audit.whatIsWrong: Four fields described Aurora's passive as a damage mark — spikes[0].text 'passive true-damage mark', spikes[2].text 'passive stacks start doing serious sustained damage', early 'mark passive chip away at your HP', wants.foe[0] 'let her passive mark do the rest of the work'.
audit.why: Spirit Abjuration does no damage of its own: 'Aurora's spells and attacks exorcise spirits from the enemies she damages. Exorcised spirits follow Aurora around and heal her.' It is a HEAL, and it heals her, not damages you.
audit.corrected: Rewrote every reference to spirits that heal her through chip damage, which also makes Grievous Wounds the actual itemisation answer.

audit.whatIsWrong: Grievous Wounds appeared nowhere on the page, in report[8].t or anywhere else.
audit.why: Her only sustain is the passive heal, and it scales with how much chip she lands — so anti-heal timing decides every extended trade in this lane.
audit.corrected: report[8].t now buys Oblivion Orb early; breakdown.feeding, breakdown.late, wants.you[0] and phases[6].why all reference it.

audit.whatIsWrong: full phases[3].side, phases[5].side and phases[6].side read 'Skill' while content win[3]='Annie', win[5]='Aurora', win[6]='Aurora' and packet.levelChart agreed with content.
audit.why: Three rows rendered two different answers. content and packet agree with each other, and with 52.35% at 701 games — Annie's window is 4-6 and Aurora scales past it.
audit.corrected: Flipped the three full sides as one group with ratings 6/4/4 and whys rewritten so the prose matches.

audit.whatIsWrong: Aurora was 'he/his' in tldr, tradeGood, tradeBad, dosFull[1].t, dontsFull[1].t and report[11].t, and no Aurora ability was ever named (packet defect).
audit.why: Aurora is female. The lane's real shape is a 900-range Twofold Hex against your 625, plus THREE separate movement tools: Across the Veil (22s leap into invisibility), The Weirding (15s backward hop) and Between Worlds.
audit.corrected: Pronouns fixed; all five ability names now appear with their cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d offered a 'fifteen-second invitation' after a spent Across the Veil, and breakdown.cooldowns had no numbers.
audit.why: Across the Veil is 22/21/20/19/18s — 22s at rank 1, not 15. The Weirding is 15/14/13/12/11s, Between Worlds 140/120/100s, Twofold Hex 9/8.5/8/7.5/7s.
audit.corrected: Corrected to twenty-two seconds and put all four cooldowns on the page.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[3] claimed she 'lacks any hard CC'.
audit.why: Her E and R both slow rather than lock down per Riot's descriptions, so the conclusion held, but stating it as an absence of CC is the kind of claim that ages badly. Note: the derived hardCC flag on R contradicts Riot's own R text, which describes only damage and a slow.
audit.corrected: Restated positively as what the abilities actually do: The Weirding and Between Worlds slow and reposition, they do not stop a point-and-click stun.

notes: Main find: Spirit Abjuration was described as a 'true-damage mark' in four fields. It is the opposite — it exorcises spirits that follow Aurora and HEAL her. That inverted the itemisation advice too: Grievous Wounds appeared nowhere despite being the single highest-value buy in the lane, so report[8].t now takes Oblivion Orb early. Second: dosFull[2].d promised a fifteen-second window off Across the Veil, which is 22s at rank 1. Level chart: full phases[3/5/6].side read 'Skill' against content and packet both; flipped as one group. Aurora was 'he' in six fields and no ability of hers was ever named (packet defect now cleared). One thing to flag: the derived hardCC flag on Between Worlds contradicts Riot's own R text, which describes only damage and a slow — I wrote to the description per the brief's rule, so the page now says it slows and repositions rather than locking you down. breakdown.wave and dontsFull[1].d remain templated.
